title: Tools Per Role: Least Privilege
objective: After this lesson you will be able to scope toolsets per role by authority, test tool selection adversarially, and audit any roster for out-of-mandate powers.
why: An agent's tools are its powers: read tools leak data, write tools act in the world, money tools move value. Granting every tool everywhere converts every confused agent into a fully-armed one — support drafting with refund execution is how incidents happen. Least privilege (exactly the tools the mandate needs, nothing more) plus selection tests is the access-control discipline of multi-agent systems.

blocks.text: Map tools to mandates: triage reads tickets; researcher searches catalogs; drafter writes text; finance executes refunds (gated); logger appends records. Each grant answers 'worst misuse?' — read-misuse leaks (scope data narrowly), write-misuse acts (gate + log), money-misuse moves value (approve first). Undifferentiated toolboxes make every agent equally dangerous.

blocks.caption: Toolsets as manifests: auditable authority per role

blocks.text: Agents choose tools from descriptions — test the choosing: present overlapping tools (lookup_order vs search_orders) with tricky tickets and assert correct selection, including refusal-to-act cases (no tool fits → ask/escalate, never force). Selection accuracy is a measured metric per role, re-run on every description edit.

blocks.caption: Power-graded tools with gating flags — audit mechanically, judge humanly

blocks.title: Audit the toolsets
blocks.note: Run it: expect exactly 1 finding — drafter holds ungated issue_refund (triage clean, finance gated-legit). One line of manifest, one incident prevented: least privilege audited, not assumed.

items: Tools follow authority: reads leak (scope data), writes act (gate+log), money moves (approve first)
Undifferentiated toolboxes make every agent equally dangerous — scope per mandate
Power-graded manifests + gating flags enable mechanical audits; selection tested adversarially

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice audit and report the finding. (b) Fix the roster (move issuance to finance@gated, drafter to read_decision only) and re-run to zero findings. (c) Add a researcher with search_catalog + read_ticket and prove the audit stays green — then state what new tool class would force a POWERS update.
hints: Baseline: 1 finding (drafter + ungated issue_refund). Fixed roster: drafter ['read_decision'], finance keeps gated issuance → 0 findings.
Researcher addition: both power-1 tools → audit stays green by construction (low-power reads need no gates).
POWERS updates when new tool classes appear (delete_user=3, external-send=2): grading is maintained, not one-off.
exercise.why: Fix-to-green plus extension-proofing practices least-privilege as maintenance: manifests audited on every roster change, power grades evolved with new capabilities. Access control is a process, not a document.
exercise.code: // Roster-change protocol: edit manifest → run audit → green required to merge.

quiz.q: Support drafter holds issue_refund ungated. Verdict?
options: Least-privilege violation: drafting ≠ executing — issuance belongs gated under finance; audit flags it
quiz.explain: Tool scope follows role authority. Execution powers in drafting roles convert confusion into incidents.

options: Grade its power (3), gate it, assign to exactly one mandated role, extend the audit — new capabilities force re-grading
quiz.explain: Power grading is maintained: every new tool gets a level, a gate decision, and an owner. Untracked powers accumulate into incidents.

quiz.q: Agents choose between lookup_order and search_orders. Testing approach?
options: Adversarial selection tests: tricky tickets asserting correct picks including refuse-to-act cases, re-run per description edit
quiz.explain: Selection is behavior: overlapping tools need measured pick accuracy, especially the no-fit refusal case. Descriptions are hypotheses; tests are proof.

summary: Scope tools by authority, grade powers, gate the dangerous, audit mechanically, test selection adversarially. Least privilege maintained per roster change.
